text:
Anya: Quick design check — compact notify preview for multi-channel. I prototyped a denser row layout so more channels fit in the preview, but noticed keyboard focus order and SR announcements feel off. thoughts? :thinking_face:

Sam: Nice, can you paste the prototype link? Also curious how the pills behave when there are 6+ channels.

Anya: https://figma.com/file/abc123/alerting-preview — the pills wrap to two rows. keyboard tab goes: preview -> first pill -> actions -> next row pill (skips some items). not great.

Priya: Repro: when pills wrap, focus is purely visual. SR reads "button" for each pill, but no context about quiet-window or route priority. We should include aria-label like `Channel: Slack (muted)` or similar.

Mike: For keyboard, we should linearize the DOM in reading order. Right now visual wrap is done with CSS flex-wrap which makes DOM order different from visual order. Might need reorder in HTML or use `order` with caution.

Anya: Good call. I tried `display:grid` with explicit template columns so DOM order = visual order, but that broke the adaptive truncate for long channel names.

Priya: Maybe show condensed names with tooltip on hover/focus. SR tooltip equivalent: use `aria-describedby` pointing to visually-hidden expanded name.

Eva: Quick copy nit: we use "Mute" in the preview action but our product copy uses "Snooze" elsewhere. We should align. Which is the canonical term?

Sam: Product prefers "Snooze" for user-facing flows. "Mute" is more technical and confuses PMs. Change preview action to "Snooze" — but keep notes for engineering (mute flag remains internal).

Anya: I'll update the mock. Also accessibility: when a user toggles suppression from the preview, there is no live region announcement. Screen reader users won't know the suppression applied. Could we add `aria-live="polite"` message like "Snoozed Slack for 1 hour"?

a11y-bot: Accessibility check list: ensure focusable pills (role="button"), aria-pressed for active state, aria-label includes channel + status, add aria-live updates on state change, maintain logical DOM order for visual wrap, contrast ratio for pill text >= 4.5:1.

Mike: Technical tradeoff — adding aria-live is easy. The tricky part is the compact pill height/contrast: current dark bg + 12px gray text is failing 4.5:1 on test. We need slightly darker text or bolder weight.

Priya: Also keyboard affordance: when opening the suppression editor from a pill, focus should land on the first control within the panel (duration select). Escape closes panel and returns focus to the pill.

Anya: Agreed. Flow: Pill focused -> Enter/Space opens drawer -> focus moves to duration select -> after action, close -> focus returns. We'll document in the interaction spec.

Sam: UI suggestion: show a subtle "preview badge" that indicates which channel would actually receive alerts given routing rules (e.g., ghosted badge for suppressed channels). This helps users debug route priority.

Eva: Love that. Might reduce confusion where a channel is enabled but won't receive alerts due to suppression/quiet window. UX: use opacity + `aria-hidden`? But need SR text like "Notifying: Email only".

Anya: Implementation note: for performance, when previewing many targets we should virtualize the list. But virtualization + `aria-live` needs careful handling so SR doesn't get flooded. We can batch announcements.

Priya: Edge case: when a user has custom channel colors, pill contrast testing must use computed color. Add runtime contrast check in the renderer and fallback to outline if contrast low.

Mike: I can add a small utility: `ensureReadableTextColor(bgColor)` that returns best foreground and flags if it fails threshold.

a11y-bot: Reminder: run automated axe checks on the preview modal and suppression drawer before shipping. Also add keyboard-only screenshots to the QA checklist.

Anya: Next steps: I'll update Figma with the grid-based layout + tooltips, swap copy to "Snooze", add aria-live messages text, and post a follow-up. Anyone want to pair on the DOM reorder PR?

Sam: I can pair tomorrow afternoon.

Mike: I'll stub the contrast util and a11y test cases.

Eva: I'll sync copy with PM and check translations for "Snooze".

Priya: I'll add the focus/ARIA acceptance criteria to the ticket.

Anya: Thanks all :raised_hands: — will post updated mock and small checklist once done.
